The best nighttime app blockers for iPhone

There is no best blocker for everyone. The useful question is whether you need a simple bedtime schedule, free customization, stronger commitment, or one system across every device.

By Hussain TaheriLast checked August 31, 202611 minute read

Publisher disclosure: Twilock publishes this page. We compare products against their official pages and help documentation, include drawbacks, and link the sources so you can verify the details yourself.

Direct answer: Twilock is the strongest fit for a narrow Night and Morning routine. ScreenZen is the standout free option. Opal and Jomo suit people who want a broader rule system. one sec is best when you want a pause before opening apps, and Apple Screen Time is the sensible built in starting point.

1. Twilock best for a focused night and morning routine

Twilock

Best for: people whose scrolling clusters around sleep

Twilock makes Night and Morning the core schedule instead of treating bedtime as one possible rule. The Night window and core streak features are free; Pro adds Morning, Strict Mode, Streak Repair, and deeper insights.

Advantages: Fast setup, clear two window model, lower current U.S. pricing, and Screen Time/app usage data that stay on device.

Drawbacks: iPhone only, each window is capped at two hours, and the morning window plus Strict Mode require Pro.

Choose it if: you want a small system that is obvious every evening rather than a general productivity suite.

2. ScreenZen best free option

ScreenZen

Best for: free customization

ScreenZen combines scheduled blocks, limits, open delays, interventions, strict blocking, streaks, and multi platform availability. Its official site describes the software as completely free and donation supported.

Advantages: No subscription, many configuration options, app and website blocking, and support for iOS, macOS, Windows, and Android.

Drawbacks: The setup surface is more complex than a two window routine, and its breadth can take time to tune.

Choose it if: cost is the deciding factor and you are willing to configure the behavior you want.

3. Opal best for broad automation

Opal

Best for: many rules across phone and computer

Opal offers Schedules, Sessions, Timers, Time Limits, Open Limits, Allow Only, scoring, and cross platform apps. It can reproduce a bedtime block and also manage workday focus.

Advantages: Flexible rule types, iPhone/Mac/Android support, polished progress features, and a documented weekly Emergency Pass for Hard Mode.

Drawbacks: Pro is substantially more expensive than Twilock or Jomo at current web prices, and the system is larger than a bedtime only use case needs.

Choose it if: you want one mature, broad attention system across multiple contexts and devices.

4. Jomo best for customization

Jomo

Best for: custom rules and unlock conditions

Jomo supports scheduled Sessions, app groups, Screen Time budgets, Strict Mode, and a wide set of unlock actions. Its pricing page lists a free tier, $29.99 annual Plus plan, and $99.99 single purchase.

Advantages: Strong feature to price ratio, iPhone and Mac support, many session types, and unusually varied unlock controls.

Drawbacks: More setup and choice than a simple bedtime blocker, and several strict/custom capabilities require Plus.

Choose it if: you enjoy tuning rules and want more flexibility than Twilock without Opal’s current price.

5. one sec best for interrupting the reflex

one sec

Best for: adding a pause before an automatic open

one sec is known for an intervention before selected apps open, and its Pro plan also includes scheduled and strict Block Sessions. The free version covers one app.

Advantages: A distinctive intervention first approach, free trial on one app, scheduled blocks, and broad platform availability for its core intervention system.

Drawbacks: Unlimited apps, recurring blocks, and strict block sessions require Pro; not every feature is available on every platform.

Choose it if: your main issue is opening an app without thinking, not only staying in it too long.

6. Apple Screen Time best built in starting point

Apple Screen Time

Best for: trying a scheduled block without another app

Downtime can schedule a broad low access period, App Limits can cap selected apps or categories, and Always Allowed protects essentials.

Advantages: Free, built into iOS, works with Family Sharing, and needs no extra account.

Drawbacks: Self managed limits can be easy to change or ignore, and the interface is not centered on a nightly commitment ritual.

Choose it if: you want to test the habit first or you are configuring a child’s device through Apple’s family controls.

How to choose

Choose Twilock if…

  • Your unwanted use clusters around sleep.
  • You want two named windows and minimal setup.
  • You prefer lower current U.S. Pro pricing.

Choose an alternative if…

  • Choose ScreenZen for a free configurable system.
  • Choose Opal or Jomo for many rule types.
  • Choose one sec for opening interventions.
  • Choose Screen Time for a built in first test.

Methodology

This is a source tested editorial comparison, not a claim that we ran every app in a controlled lab. We checked current official sites, help centers, and App Store information for five factors: nighttime scheduling, strength/escape behavior, free tier usefulness, current price, and platform scope. We do not use vendor outcome claims, review counts, or affiliate commissions to rank the products.

Frequently asked questions

What is the best free nighttime app blocker?
ScreenZen offers the broadest free third party feature set in this comparison. Apple Screen Time is the best built in option. Twilock’s Night window is also free if you want a more focused routine.
Which blocker is hardest to bypass?
“Strict” means different things across apps and iOS versions. Review the exact exit, emergency, uninstall, and Screen Time permission behavior before committing. Our strict blocker guide compares those differences.
Can these apps block websites as well as apps?
Opal, Jomo, ScreenZen, one sec, Freedom, and Apple Screen Time offer website controls in at least some configurations. Twilock is positioned around the apps or categories selected with Apple’s Screen Time picker.
Do I need to pay for a bedtime schedule?
No. Apple Screen Time, ScreenZen, and Twilock’s Night window provide free ways to schedule nighttime protection.

Protect tonight.

Twilock focuses on the two windows around sleep, with Strict Mode when you want your earlier choice to hold.
